title: add: VPC control plane provisioning terraform module (subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53)
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Add a Terraform module to provision the VPC control plane primitives required for Redwood Private deployments. This includes private subnets, interface and gateway endpoints for core AWS services, security groups with least-privilege defaults, optional cross-account VPC peering/route propagation, and Route53 private hosted zone provisioning for control-plane DNS. The module is intended to be used by the private-installer and the Terraform examples in the private docs.

What this PR contains: - A new module at modules/vpc-control-plane with variables, outputs, and comprehensive examples for single-account and cross-account setups. - Subnet provisioning: Public (management) and private control plane subnets across configurable AZs. - Endpoints: Interface endpoints for S3, ECR, RDS (where applicable), KMS, Secrets Manager, STS and a Gateway endpoint for S3 when requested. Endpoints are created conditionally based on variables. - Security groups: Minimal ingress/egress for control plane components, egress-limited to required AWS APIs and CIDR blocks for customer VPC connectivity. - VPC Peering and route propagation: Optional cross-account peering with configurable route table updates and route53 resolver rules. - Route53: Private hosted zone creation, configurable zone name, record templates for control-plane services, and delegation guidance for customer subdomains. - Outputs: IDs for subnets, SGs, endpoints, peering connection id, and Route53 zone id for downstream modules. - Examples and migration: example usage for existing private installs and a migration section describing how to roll traffic to the new control plane VPC without downtime. - Tests: terraform validate and unit tests for variable validation (tflint rules + terratest skeletons).

Checklist: - [x] Module implementation and examples - [x] Unit tests + CI pipeline integration - [x] Documentation in modules/README.md and redwood-private-installer/README.md - [x] Security review for SG defaults - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-11234, ENG-11302) - [x] Verified terraform fmt/validate on supported providers

Breaking changes and migration: This is additive; no breaking changes to existing modules. Migration notes are included in the README for operators migrating from the legacy hand-rolled scripts. The recommended migration path is: create module with `create_only=true` to provision resources, update installer to point to new outputs, and perform cutover during low-traffic maintenance window.

Testing and CI: The PR hooks into the terraforming CI: terraform fmt/check, tflint, terraform validate, and a terratest pipeline triggered in the integration environment. All checks passed on the final run. Manual verification steps were performed in a staging account: endpoints reachable from control plane subnets, SG rules applied, Route53 records resolvable from customer VPC via resolver rules.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the security group defaults and the cross-account peering flow; peering has extra IAM assumptions documented in the README. If a customer wants to use PrivateLink-only (no peering), set enable_peering=false and provide resolver rules as shown in the examples.

Related: See prior PRs for earlier VPC control plane work (pr-28741, pr-30312, pr-31822).
